proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(f_{\ell 1}=p_\ell\) and \(f_{\ell0}=1-p_\ell\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}eta\text{-}interior}\), all \(p_\ell,1-p_\ell,q_0,q_1,e_\ell,1-e_\ell\) are positive, so every division below is legitimate.

Fix \(\ell\) and set \(s_\ell=p_\ell\lambda _1(\ell,1)\).  The normalization in \(\mathrm{ass{:}normalization\text{-}one}\) gives
\[
 \lambda _1(\ell,0)=\frac{1-s_\ell}{1-p_\ell}.
\]
The two box restrictions in \(\mathrm{ass{:}ratio\text{-}box\text{-}one}\) are therefore equivalent to
\[
 \max\!\left\{\frac{p_\ell}{G},,1-G(1-p_\ell)\right\}
 \leq s_\ell\leq
 \min\!\left\{Gp_\ell,,1-\frac{1-p_\ell}{G}\right\},
\]
which is exactly \(D_G(p_\ell)\leq s_\ell\leq U_G(p_\ell)\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}envelope\text{-}maps}\).  This equivalence is reversible.

Next observe, using the first normalization, that
\[
 \sum_{y=0}^1 f_{\ell y}\rho_\ell(y)
 =e_\ell+(1-e_\ell)\sum_{y=0}^1f_{\ell y}\lambda _1(\ell,y)=1.
\]
The success mass of this normalized binary distribution is
\[
 f_{\ell1}\rho_\ell(1)
 =e_\ell p_\ell+(1-e_\ell)p_\ell\lambda _1(\ell,1)
 =e_\ell p_\ell+(1-e_\ell)s_\ell=:r_\ell.
\]
Because \(0<e_\ell,p_\ell,s_\ell<1\), one has \(0<r_\ell<1\).  Set \(t_\ell=r_\ell\lambda _{0Y}(\ell,1)\).  Applying the preceding binary calculation with \((p_\ell,G,s_\ell)\) replaced by \((r_\ell,B,t_\ell)\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}normalization\text{-}outcome}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}ratio\text{-}box\text{-}outcome}\) are equivalent to
\[
 D_B(r_\ell)\leq t_\ell\leq U_B(r_\ell),\qquad
 \lambda _{0Y}(\ell,1)=\frac{t_\ell}{r_\ell},\qquad
 \lambda _{0Y}(\ell,0)=\frac{1-t_\ell}{1-r_\ell}.
\]

Finally put \(h=q_0\lambda _{0L}(0)\).  The covariate normalization gives
\[
 \lambda _{0L}(0)=\frac h{q_0},\qquad
 \lambda _{0L}(1)=\frac{1-h}{q_1},
\]
and the covariate box is equivalent to \(D_C(q_0)\leq h\leq U_C(q_0)\).  Thus the forward map has precisely the stated product of intervals.  The displayed inverse formulas are unique, satisfy all three normalizations by substitution, and satisfy all three boxes by the definitions of \(D_K\) and \(U_K\).  Hence the map and the compatible ratio lift are mutually inverse, proving the bijection.

Define the identified set without conflating it with an observed-law functional:
\[
 \Theta_I(P)=\left\{\mathbb E_Q[Y^{1,1}]:
 Q\text{ has observed marginal }P,\ Q\text{ obeys the two consistency assumptions, and its ratios lie in }\mathcal R(P;G,B,C)\right\}.
\]
The cited compatibility-program lemma identifies this set as the image of the reduced feasible set from \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}probability\text{-}reduction}\) under
\[
 M(s,t,h)=a\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell r_\ell
 +(1-a)\{h t_0+(1-h)t_1\},\qquad
 r_\ell=e_\ell p_\ell+(1-e_\ell)s_\ell.
\]
This invocation uses Tan's compatibility result only to relate the causal full-data laws to the observed-law program; the optimization below is derived directly.

The reduced feasible set is nonempty because \(s_\ell=p_\ell\), \(r_\ell=p_\ell\), \(t_\ell=p_\ell\), and \(h=q_0\) are feasible.  It is compact.  It is also convex: besides interval constraints on \(s_\ell\) and \(h\), the restrictions on \((r_\ell,t_\ell)\) are the four linear inequalities
\[
 t_\ell\geq r_\ell/B,\quad t_\ell\geq Br_\ell-(B-1),\quad
 t_\ell\leq Br_\ell,\quad t_\ell\leq 1-(1-r_\ell)/B.
\]
Consequently it is connected, and its continuous real-valued image under \(M\) is a compact interval.

For the upper endpoint, \(0<h<1\) because \(0<q_0<1\) and \(C<\infty\).  Thus, at fixed \((s,h)\), both coefficients of \(t_0,t_1\) in \(M\) are strictly positive, so \(t_\ell=U_B(r_\ell)\).  Both affine pieces defining \(U_B\) have positive slope, hence \(U_B\) is increasing.  The coefficient \(a q_\ell\) of \(r_\ell\) is positive, and therefore the resulting objective is increasing in each \(r_\ell\) and in each \(s_\ell\).  It follows that
\[
 s_\ell=U_G(p_\ell),\quad r_\ell=r_\ell^+,\quad t_\ell=t_\ell^+.
\]
The remaining function of \(h\) is affine, so its maximum over \([h^-,h^+]\) is attained at one of the two endpoints.  This gives exactly \(F_+(P)\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\text{-}sharp\text{-}endpoints}\).  Reversing every monotonicity step gives \(s_\ell=D_G(p_\ell)\), \(r_\ell=r_\ell^-\), \(t_\ell=t_\ell^-\), and the endpoint of \([h^-,h^+]\) minimizing the last affine expression; hence the lower value is exactly \(F_-(P)\).

Compactness gives reduced optimizers.  The compatible ratio lift maps each optimizer into \(\mathcal R(P;G,B,C)\), with positive denominators by the interior assumption.  The cited compatibility-program lemma then supplies a full-data law having the complete observed marginal \(P\) and attaining the corresponding causal mean.  Since the continuous image is an interval, every value between the two attained extrema is also attained.  Therefore
\[
 \Theta_I(P)=[F_-(P),F_+(P)],
\]
so these are sharp bounds, not merely outer bounds.

It remains to verify the finite atlas.  Each of \(U_G(p_0),U_G(p_1),U_B(r_0^+),U_B(r_1^+)\) selects the smaller of two affine pieces; the ordering of \(t_0^+,t_1^+\) selects \(h^-\) or \(h^+\); and the selected covariate envelope selects one of its two affine pieces.  These are six binary choices.  The weak inequalities in \(\mathcal B_+(P)\) are exactly the conditions that the chosen pieces and ordering are active, so substitution gives \(F_+(P)=f_\beta^+(P)\) for an admissible \(\beta\), among at most \(2^6=64\) rational formulas.  The same argument, with maxima of the lower affine pieces and the minimizing ordering, gives \(\mathcal B_-(P)\) and at most \(64\) lower formulas.  At a piece tie the two affine values coincide; at an ordering tie \(t_0^s=t_1^s\), the final affine expression is independent of \(h\).  Thus every simultaneously active tied branch has the same endpoint value.

For a law \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), the seven cell probabilities factor as
\[
 z_\varnothing=1-a,\qquad
 z_{\ell\mathrm N}=a q_\ell(1-e_\ell),\qquad
 z_{\ell y}=a q_\ell e_\ell p_\ell^y(1-p_\ell)^{1-y}.
\]
Every factor is positive by \(\mathrm{ass{:}eta\text{-}interior}\).  Hence
\[
 d_\ell=z_{\ell\mathrm N}+z_{\ell0}+z_{\ell1}=a q_\ell,\qquad
 m_\ell=z_{\ell0}+z_{\ell1}=a q_\ell e_\ell,\qquad
 z_{\ell1}=a q_\ell e_\ell p_\ell.
\]
The coordinate definitions therefore give
\[
 a(z)=a,\quad q_\ell(z)=q_\ell,\quad e_\ell(z)=e_\ell,\quad p_\ell(z)=p_\ell,
\]
which proves the asserted identity for \(\psi(z)\).  Direct substitution of these seven equalities into every formula in \(\mathrm{def{:}seven\text{-}cell\text{-}simplex\text{-}extensions}\) gives, successively,
\[
 \widetilde r_{\ell\beta}^s(z)=r_{\ell\beta}^s,\quad
 \widetilde t_{\ell\beta}^s(z)=t_{\ell\beta}^s,\quad
 \widetilde h_\beta(z)=h_\beta,\quad
 \widetilde f_\beta^s(z)=f_\beta^s(P).
\]
The same substitution in the compact envelope formulas yields \(\widetilde F_s(z)=F_s(P)\).  Finally, the sharp-frontier theorem and the weak branch rules imply equality with every branch in \(\mathcal B_s(P)\).  Because tied affine pieces agree at their common face and the final expression is independent of \(h\) when its two stratum values tie, this conclusion includes every active tie.

We first derive the elementary check-transform facts used in both components.  For \(K>1\), \(u\in(0,1)\), \(k\in[0,1]\), and \(W\sim\operatorname{Bern}(u)\), direct evaluation at \(W=0,1\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E[T_K(W,k)]
 =Ku+(1-K^{-1})\{1-(K+1)u\}k.
\]
Thus its minimum over \(k\in[0,1]\) is \(U_K(u)\), and the minimizer set is
\[
 \mathcal Q_K(u)=
 \begin{cases}
 \{0\},&u<(K+1)^{-1},\\
 [0,1],&u=(K+1)^{-1},\\
 \{1\},&u>(K+1)^{-1}.
 \end{cases}
\]
For \(K=1\), \(T_1(x,k)=x\).  The map \(x\mapsto T_K(x,k)\) is increasing and convex, strictly increasing for finite \(K\), and it obeys the affine-equivariance identity
\[
 T_K(b+d x,b+d k)=b+dT_K(x,k)\qquad(d\geq0).
\]
All these claims follow by comparing the two displayed affine pieces in \(\mathrm{def{:}check\text{-}transform}\).

We shall also use the following binary dual identity, derived rather than assumed.  If \(v_0,v_1\in[0,1]\), then affine equivariance and the preceding Bernoulli calculation give
\[
 \min_{c\in[0,1]}\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell T_C(v_\ell,c)
 =\max_{h\in[D_C(q_0),U_C(q_0)]}\{h v_0+(1-h)v_1\}=R_C(v).
\]
Indeed, if \(v_0\leq v_1\), write \(v_L=v_0+(v_1-v_0)W\) with \(W\sim\operatorname{Bern}(q_1)\); clipping \(c\) to \([v_0,v_1]\) cannot increase the objective, and the minimum is \(v_0+(v_1-v_0)U_C(q_1)\).  The identity \(1-U_C(q_1)=D_C(q_0)\) gives the right side.  The case \(v_0\geq v_1\) is symmetric.

For the first conservative component, abbreviate \(r_\ell=r_\ell^+\), \(z_0(k)=(1-B^{-1})k\), \(z_1(k)=B-(B-1)k\), and
\[
 m_\ell(k)=(1-r_\ell)z_0(k)+r_\ell z_1(k).
\]
The Bernoulli calculation with \(K=B\) shows \(m_\ell(k)\geq U_B(r_\ell)=t_\ell^+\).  Conditional Jensen, followed by strict monotonicity, gives for every \(c,k_0,k_1\),
\[
 (1-r_\ell)T_C(z_0(k_\ell),c)+r_\ell T_C(z_1(k_\ell),c)
 \geq T_C(m_\ell(k_\ell),c)\geq T_C(t_\ell^+,c).
\]
After summing with positive \(q_\ell\), minimizing, and applying the binary dual identity, the second term of \(V_1^+\) is at least \(R_C(t^+)\).  Hence \(V_1^+\geq F_+(P)\).

If \(C=1\), then \(T_C(x,c)=x\), each \(k_\ell\) can attain \(m_\ell=t_\ell^+\), and the dual identity reduces to \(R_1(t)=\sum q_\ell t_\ell\).  Therefore \(V_1^+=F_+(P)\).  Conversely suppose \(C>1\) and equality holds.  Positivity gives \(0<r_\ell<1\), while \(z_0(k)<z_1(k)\).  Equality in conditional Jensen for the two-slope convex map \(T_C(\cdot,c)\) requires
\[
 c\notin(z_0(k_\ell),z_1(k_\ell))
\]
for both strata, and strict monotonicity requires \(m_\ell(k_\ell)=t_\ell^+\).  All support intervals share a nonempty open interval: it is \((0,1)\) when \(B=1\), and it contains \((1-B^{-1},1)\) when \(B>1\).  Because \(z_0(k)\leq1-B^{-1}<1\leq z_1(k)\) in the latter case, a common \(c\) outside both open support intervals must lie on the same side of both.  Since each \(m_\ell\) is strictly between its two support points, either \(c<t_\ell^+\) for both strata or \(c>t_\ell^+\) for both.  In the first case increasing \(c\) slightly strictly decreases \(\sum q_\ell T_C(t_\ell^+,c)\); in the second, decreasing it does so.  Thus such a \(c\) cannot attain the binary dual minimum, a contradiction.  Compactness of \([0,1]^3\) turns nonattainment of equality into \(V_1^+>F_+(P)\).  We have proved
\[
 V_1^+=F_+(P)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C=1.
\]

For the second component, let \(S\sim\operatorname{Bern}(p_\ell)\).  The first Bernoulli calculation gives
\[
 A_\ell(c)=e_\ell p_\ell+(1-e_\ell)\mathbb E[T_G(S,c)]\geq r_\ell^+.
\]
For fixed \(k\), put \(Z=z_0(k)+(z_1(k)-z_0(k))S=T_B(S,k)\).  Affine equivariance yields
\[
 \min_c\mathbb E[T_G(Z,c)]
 =z_0(k)+\{z_1(k)-z_0(k)\}U_G(p_\ell).
\]
Consequently
\[
 D_\ell(k,c)
 \geq z_0(k)+\{z_1(k)-z_0(k)\}r_\ell^+
 =m_\ell(k)\geq t_\ell^+.
\]
Every \(h\in[h^-,h^+]\) lies strictly between zero and one.  Hence \(R_C\) is strictly increasing in each coordinate.  Since \(a,1-a,q_0,q_1>0\), equality \(V_2^+=F_+(P)\) is therefore equivalent to the existence, separately in each stratum, of \((k,c)\) for which both \(A_\ell(c)=r_\ell^+\) and \(D_\ell(k,c)=t_\ell^+\).

Assume \(G,B>1\).  If \(p_\ell<(G+1)^{-1}\), equality in \(A_\ell\geq r_\ell^+\) uniquely requires \(c=0\), whereas equality in the first inequality for \(D_\ell\) requires \(c=z_0(k)\).  These requirements intersect exactly when \(k=0\).  Equality in \(m_\ell(k)\geq U_B(r_\ell^+)\) allows \(k=0\) exactly when \(r_\ell^+\leq(B+1)^{-1}\), including equality.  If \(p_\ell>(G+1)^{-1}\), the two required thresholds are \(c=1\) and \(c=z_1(k)\); they intersect exactly when \(k=1\), which minimizes \(m_\ell\) exactly when \(r_\ell^+\geq(B+1)^{-1}\).  If \(p_\ell=(G+1)^{-1}\), every normalized threshold between the two support points minimizes the transformed expectation, and the two threshold sets intersect for every minimizing \(k\).  If \(r_\ell^+=(B+1)^{-1}\), every \(k\in[0,1]\) minimizes \(m_\ell\).  Combining the four cases gives precisely
\[
 \bigl(p_\ell-(G+1)^{-1}\bigr)
 \bigl(r_\ell^+-(B+1)^{-1}\bigr)\geq0.
\]
The choices are stratum-specific, so equality holds exactly when this weak inequality holds for both \(\ell=0,1\).  If \(G=1\), then \(H_\ell(x,c)=x\), so the shared-threshold restriction disappears and minimization over \(k\) attains \(t_\ell^+\).  If \(B=1\), then \(T_B(S,k)=S\), so the same \(c\) minimizing \(A_\ell\) also minimizes \(D_\ell=A_\ell\).  Thus these two sensitivity-free faces are exactly the additional equality cases.

Both conservative components dominate \(F_+\), and \(V^+=\min(V_1^+,V_2^+)\).  It follows that \(V^+=F_+\) exactly on the union stated in the theorem; on its complement both compactly attained components are strictly larger, so their minimum is strictly larger.

For the lower endpoint replace \(Y\) by \(1-Y\).  The envelope identities
\[
 U_K(1-x)=1-D_K(x),\qquad
 r_\ell^+(1-p_\ell)=1-r_\ell^-(p_\ell)
\]
and the definitions \(V_j^-(p)=1-V_j^+(1-p)\) transfer every equality and strictness statement.  The upper product condition becomes
\[
 \left(p_\ell-\frac{G}{G+1}\right)
 \left(r_\ell^--\frac{B}{B+1}\right)\geq0.
\]
The \(C=1\), \(G=1\), and \(B=1\) faces transfer unchanged, and reversing the upper strict inequality gives \(V^-<F_-\).  All case boundaries were treated by weak inequalities, so active ties are included.

At the displayed law, the envelope calculations are exact:
\[
 U_2(3/10)=3/5,\quad U_2(4/5)=9/10,\quad
 r^+=(9/20,17/20),\quad t^+=(29/40,37/40),\quad
 (h^-,h^+)=(1/4,3/4).
\]
Because \(t_0^+<t_1^+\), the maximizing covariate weight is \(h^-\).  Hence
\[
 F_+(P)=\frac12\frac{(9/20+17/20)}2
 +\frac12\left\{\frac14\frac{29}{40}+\frac34\frac{37}{40}\right\}
 =\frac{13}{40}+\frac7{16}=\frac{61}{80}.
\]

We next certify the first program without numerical optimization.  For \(K=2\),
\[
 z_0(k)=k/2,\qquad z_1(k)=2-k,\qquad
 T_2(z,c)\geq z/2+c/2,\quad T_2(z,c)\geq2z-c.
\]
Use the first lower affine piece at \(z_0\) and the second at \(z_1\).  The coefficient of each \(k_\ell\) in the resulting lower bound is \(q_\ell(1-9r_\ell^+)/4<0\), and the coefficient of the common \(c\) is
\[
 \sum_\ell q_\ell\{(1-r_\ell^+)/2-r_\ell^+\}
 =\frac12-\frac32\frac{13}{20}<0.
\]
Thus the lower bound is minimized at \(k_0=k_1=c=1\), where the selected affine pieces are active and the bound is attained.  Its value is
\[
 \sum_\ell q_\ell\left(\frac34+\frac{r_\ell^+}{4}\right)
 =\frac34+\frac{13}{80}=\frac{73}{80}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 V_1^+=\frac{13}{40}+\frac12\frac{73}{80}=\frac{25}{32}.
\]

For the second program, write \(A_\ell=A_\ell(c_\ell)\) and \(D_\ell=D_\ell(k_\ell,c_\ell)\).  Since
\[
 R_2(D_0,D_1)\geq\frac14D_0+\frac34D_1,
\]
every feasible value is at least
\[
 \left(\frac14A_0+\frac18D_0\right)
 +\left(\frac14A_1+\frac38D_1\right).
\]
The general inequalities in the conservative-frontier proof give \(A_1\geq17/20\) and \(D_1\geq37/40\), simultaneously attained at \(c_1=k_1=1\).  The second parenthesis is therefore at least \(179/320\).

For stratum zero, direct calculation with
\[
 H(x,c)=\max\{3x/2-c/2,,3x/4+c/4\}
\]
gives \(A_0(c)=9/20+c/40\).  Minimizing \(D_0(k,c)\) over \(k\in[0,1]\) gives
\[
 \min_kD_0(k,c)=
 \begin{cases}
 9/10-7c/20,&0\leq c\leq1/2,\\
 57/80+c/40,&1/2\leq c\leq1.
 \end{cases}
\]
To verify this display, note that \(z_1(k)\geq c\), while the active piece at \(z_0(k)=k/2\) changes at \(k=2c\); the objective decreases up to that point and increases afterward when \(c\leq1/2\), whereas for \(c\geq1/2\) it decreases through \(k=1\).  Therefore
\[
 2A_0(c)+D_0(k,c)\geq\frac{33}{20},
\]
with equality at \(c_0=1/2,k_0=1\).  The first parenthesis is at least \(33/160\).  At these four thresholds, \((D_0,D_1)=(29/40,37/40)\), so the displayed face \(h=1/4\) of \(R_2\) is active.  Hence the lower bound is attained and
\[
 V_2^+=\frac{33}{160}+\frac{179}{320}=\frac{49}{64}.
\]
Thus \(V^+=49/64\) and
\[
 V^+-F_+(P)=\frac{49}{64}-\frac{61}{80}=\frac1{320}>0.
\]
Moreover, \(V_1^+-V_2^+=1/64>0\), so the exact ordering is
\[
 F_+(P)<V_2^+=V^+<V_1^+.
\]

Finally, every envelope and check-transform is continuous.  Each conservative value is the minimum of a jointly continuous function over a fixed compact cube, so the elementary inequality
\[
 \left|\min_u g(x,u)-\min_u g(x',u)\right|
 \leq\sup_u|g(x,u)-g(x',u)|
\]
shows that \(V_1^+\) and \(V_2^+\) are continuous in the primitive probabilities and sensitivity constants.  The compact sharp formula is continuous as well.  Both strict gaps in the last ordering therefore persist on a relative neighborhood.  At the witness the smallest primitive probability or complement is \(1/5\); hence, for every \(\eta<1/5\), that neighborhood can be chosen inside \(\mathcal M_\eta\).

Let \(\delta=\eta^4/2\) and
\[
 K_\delta=\{z\in\Delta_6:\min_jz_j\geq\delta\}.
\]
This set is compact and convex.  The denominators \(a(z)\), \(d_\ell(z)\), and \(m_\ell(z)\) in the coordinate map are sums of coordinates and are bounded below on \(K_\delta\).  Hence every rational branch formula extends to a twice continuously differentiable function on a neighborhood of \(K_\delta\).  Because there are only \(128\) signed branches, there is a finite \(H=H(\eta,G,B,C)\) such that every branch Hessian has operator norm at most \(H\) there.

Fix a sign \(s\), put \(v=z'-z\), and parameterize the segment by \(z_u=z+uv\), \(0\leq u\leq1\).  The compact endpoint formula is obtained by finitely many minima and maxima of affine pieces.  It is therefore Lipschitz on \(K_\delta\), and along the segment it is absolutely continuous.  At almost every \(u\), it agrees locally with an active rational branch, say \(\widetilde f_{\beta(u)}^s\), and
\[
 \frac{d}{du}\widetilde F_s(z_u)
 =\nabla\widetilde f_{\beta(u)}^s(z_u)^\top v.
\]
If the segment lies in a tie face, all branches agreeing on that face have the same directional derivative along the face, so the same formula remains valid almost everywhere.  Taylor's theorem and the uniform Hessian bound give
\[
 \left|\{\nabla\widetilde f_{\beta(u)}^s(z_u)-
 \nabla\widetilde f_{\beta(u)}^s(z)\}^\top v\right|
 \leq Hu\|v\|_2^2.
\]
Integrating and using the fundamental theorem for absolutely continuous functions yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widetilde F_s(z')-\widetilde F_s(z)|
 &\leq \int_0^1
 \left|\nabla\widetilde f_{
 \beta(u)}^s(z)^\top v\right|\,du
 +\frac H2\|v\|_2^2\\
 &\leq\max_{\beta\in\{0,1\}^6}
 \left|\nabla\widetilde f_\beta^s(z)^\top(z'-z)\right|
 +\frac H2\|z'-z\|_2^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Taking \(M=H/2\) proves the asserted uniform inequality.  The argument neither selects a unique branch nor divides by a score variance, so redundant branches, coincident gradients, and crossings of any number of faces require no additional condition.

Let \(z=z(P)\).  The cell factorizations in \(\mathrm{lem{:}seven\text{-}cell\text{-}simplex\text{-}agreement}\) and the interior assumption imply
\[
 z_\varnothing\geq\eta,\qquad z_{\ell\mathrm N}\geq\eta^3,\qquad
 z_{\ell y}\geq\eta^4.
\]
Thus all true seven-cell probabilities are at least \(\eta^4\).  Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound over seven cells give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\eta}P(E_n^c)
 \leq14\exp(-n\eta^8/2)\longrightarrow0.
\]

Index all \(128\) gradients by \(j=(s,\beta)\), write
\[
 g_j(z)=\nabla\widetilde f_\beta^s(z),\qquad
 S_n(z)=\max_j\left|g_j(z)^\top\sqrt n(\widehat z-z)\right|,\qquad
 \Sigma(z)=\operatorname{diag}(z)-zz^\top.
\]
On \(K_{\eta^4/2}\), the preceding rational smoothness argument gives a common finite bound on all \(g_j\) and their first derivatives.

We next establish the multiplier calibration, including singular cases.  Conditional on the data,
\[
 \mathbb G_n^*\sim N(0,\Sigma(\widehat z)),
\]
exactly, because the multipliers are Gaussian and
\(n^{-1}\sum_i(X_i-\widehat z)(X_i-\widehat z)^\top
=\Sigma(\widehat z)\).  Therefore \(c_n\) is the conditional quantile of a finite Gaussian maximum whose coefficient array and covariance are continuous functions of \(\widehat z\).

The limiting maximum is never degenerate.  At every \(z=z(P)\), choose any active upper branch.  Shift probability infinitesimally from cell \(z_{00}\) to \(z_{01}\), holding their sum fixed.  This changes only \(p_0\) among the primitive coordinates.  Along an active upper branch,
\[
 \frac{\partial f_\beta^+}{\partial p_0}
 \geq a q_0/G\geq\eta^2/G,
\]
because every active envelope slope is positive and the first sharp-objective term alone has this derivative lower bound.  Since \(m_0(z)\leq1\), the two corresponding cell-gradient coordinates differ by at least \(\eta^2/G\).  Both cell probabilities are at least \(\eta^4\), so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_z\{g_j(z)^\top(X-z)\}
 \geq \eta^{12}/G^2>0
\]
for that active branch.  Other coordinates may have zero variance and \(\Sigma(z)\) is necessarily singular in the all-ones direction; neither affects this lower bound for the maximum.

For completeness, uniform Gaussian approximation can be proved by a subsequence argument, avoiding any hidden nonsingularity premise.  Given any sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal M_\eta\), compactness supplies a subsequence with \(z(P_n)\to z_\infty\).  For fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^7\), boundedness of the categorical summands and the expansion \(\log(1+x)=x-x^2/2+o(x^2)\), uniformly for \(x=O(n^{-1/2})\), give
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_n}\exp\{it^\top\sqrt n(\widehat z-z(P_n))\}
 \longrightarrow \exp\{-t^\top\Sigma(z_\infty)t/2\}.
\]
Thus the triangular-array multinomial vector converges to \(Z_\infty\sim N(0,\Sigma(z_\infty))\), even when this covariance is singular.  Continuity of the finite gradient array gives
\[
 S_n(z(P_n))\ \Longrightarrow\ S_\infty:=
 \max_j|g_j(z_\infty)^\top Z_\infty|.
\]
Also \(\widehat z-z(P_n)\to0\) in probability uniformly, so the conditional law of the multiplier maximum converges in probability to the law of the same \(S_\infty\).

The distribution of \(S_\infty\) is continuous: for \(x>0\), its level set is contained in a finite union of level sets of nondegenerate one-dimensional Gaussian linear forms, after zero-variance forms are discarded; at zero, the uniformly nondegenerate active coordinate gives probability zero.  It is strictly increasing on \((0,\infty)\), because the maximum is a nonzero continuous homogeneous seminorm on the Gaussian support, and every nonempty relative open annulus has positive Gaussian probability.  Hence its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile is unique and positive.  Conditional quantile convergence now gives, along the arbitrary subsequence,
\[
 P_{P_n}\{S_n(z(P_n))\leq c_n\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
The sequential compactness argument proves this convergence uniformly over \(\mathcal M_\eta\).

On \(E_n\), apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}branch\text{-}remainder}\) to \(z\) and \(\widehat z\), for both signs.  With its constant \(M\),
\[
 \max_{s\in\{-,+\}}|\widetilde F_s(\widehat z)-\widetilde F_s(z)|
 \leq \frac{S_n(z)}{\sqrt n}+M\|\widehat z-z\|_2^2.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \sup_P P_P\{M\|\widehat z-z\|_2^2>n^{-3/4}\}
 \leq M n^{-1/4}\sup_P\mathbb E_P\|\sqrt n(\widehat z-z)\|_2^2
 \leq M n^{-1/4}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus, with limiting probability at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly, both endpoint errors are at most \(w_n=c_n/\sqrt n+n^{-3/4}\).  The simplex-agreement lemma identifies the true endpoints with \(F_-(P),F_+(P)\), and the fallback interval covers them automatically.  Clipping at zero and one preserves containment.  Therefore
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_\eta}
 P\{[F_-(P),F_+(P)]\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]

Finally, bounded gradients and \(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma(\widehat z)\leq1\) imply by a union Gaussian tail bound that, on \(E_n\), \(c_n\) is bounded by a constant depending only on \((\eta,G,B,C,\alpha)\).  Hence \(w_n=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly.  No inverse covariance, studentization, or deletion of redundant coordinates has been used, which proves the stated robustness to ties, singular covariance, and zero-variance branch coordinates.

When \(K=1\), the definitions give \(D_1(x)=U_1(x)=x\).  Therefore \(G=B=C=1\) implies, for each \(\ell\),
\[
 r_\ell^-=r_\ell^+=e_\ell p_\ell+(1-e_\ell)p_\ell=p_\ell,\qquad
 t_\ell^-=t_\ell^+=p_\ell,\qquad h^-=h^+=q_0.
\]
Substitution into either compact endpoint gives
\[
 F_-(P)=F_+(P)
 =a\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell p_\ell
 +(1-a)\{q_0p_0+q_1p_1\}
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell p_\ell.
\]
By the sharp-frontier theorem, the causal identified set is the singleton containing this observed-law functional.  Under the two consistency assumptions it is precisely the ordinary two-period g-formula for \(\mu_{11}\), completing the sanity reduction.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix a positive observed binary law \(P\) and finite \(G,B,C\geq 1\).  Under target-strategy consistency, Tan's Lemmas 7--8 imply the following two facts.  First, a triple \((\lambda _1,\lambda _{0Y},\lambda _{0L})\) is induced by a full-data law compatible with the complete observed marginal \(P\) if and only if it belongs to \(\mathcal R(P;G,B,C)\).  Second, after writing \(s_\ell=p_\ell\lambda _1(\ell,1)\), \(r_\ell=e_\ell p_\ell+(1-e_\ell)s_\ell\), \(t_\ell=r_\ell\lambda _{0Y}(\ell,1)\), and \(h=q_0\lambda _{0L}(0)\), the compatible law has
\[
 \mathbb E[Y^{1,1}]
 =a\sum_{\ell=0}^1q_\ell r_\ell
 +(1-a)\{h t_0+(1-h)t_1\}.
\]
Conversely, every value of this display generated by a ratio triple in \(\mathcal R(P;G,B,C)\) is attained by such a compatible full-data law.

proposed.statement: For every observed law in \(\mathcal M_\eta\), the sharp identified set for \(\mu_{11}\) under Tan's product sensitivity model is exactly \([F_-(P),F_+(P)]\). Both endpoints have the compact formulas in \(\mathrm{def{:}compact\text{-}sharp\text{-}endpoints}\), each is evaluable by at most \(64\) rational branches with the weak branch inequalities in \(\mathcal B_-(P)\) and \(\mathcal B_+(P)\), every active tie gives the same endpoint value, and each endpoint is attained by a full-data law compatible with the complete observed law \(P\).
proposed.justification: It replaces an implicit coupled sharp program by a closed-form, fully attainable binary frontier.
proposed.gap: Tan (2025), Lemma 8, gives the exact compatible-law optimization but states that ratio coupling obstructs a general exact unconstrained representation; no finite binary formula is given.
proposed.consumer: Dickerman et al.'s six-year cancer analysis can report a sharp interval for the absolute risk under a sustained metformin strategy after binary coarsening.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses Tan's published exact compatibility and compatible-law objective as a load-bearing premise, so that cited leaf must be declared explicitly in the dependency spine.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A complete contact-set directional-multiplier construction satisfying uniform coverage, pointwise exactness at every continuous limiting contact quantile, first-order domination of the all-branch interval, and strict improvement on a certified nonempty observable region.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen contact-set definition is only a handle.  Screening inclusion and unique-branch reduction follow from the finite rational atlas, but uniform calibration along root-\(n\) local approaches to multiway faces requires a directional critical-value theorem that remains valid with singular and vanishing scores.  Strict narrowing at the fixed \(1-\alpha\) quantile additionally requires a strict stochastic-quantile comparison, which is not implied merely by deleting an inactive score.
open_obligations.attempted: Screened branches at tolerance \(\kappa_n/\sqrt n\) with \(\kappa_n\to\infty\) and \(\kappa_n/\sqrt n\to0\); used uniform Lipschitz control to retain all locally reachable active branches and compared the screened multiplier maximum pointwise with the all-branch maximum.  This proves the inclusion and unique-separated-branch parts but does not close the joint uniform directional-quantile and strictness assertions.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(\kappa_n\to\infty\) with \(\kappa_n/\sqrt n\to0\), and screen by
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal A}_s=
 \left\{\beta:\left|\widetilde f_\beta^s(\widehat z)-
 \widetilde F_s(\widehat z)\right|\leq\kappa_n/\sqrt n\right\}.
\]
Uniform Lipschitz bounds and root-\(n\) tightness imply that every branch active at the true law, and every branch reachable along the segment from \(z\) to \(\widehat z\), belongs to \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_s\) with probability tending to one uniformly.  A multiplier maximum over these screened scores is pointwise no larger than the all-branch maximum; at a law with a unique branch separated by a positive value gap, the screen selects that branch with probability tending to one.  What remains unproved is a single calibrated directional critical value that simultaneously (i) preserves this inclusion uniformly along all \(n^{-1/2}\)-local approaches to multiway faces with singular scores, (ii) has exact limiting coverage at every continuous contact-set quantile, and (iii) has a rigorously certified strict quantile reduction on a nonempty observable region at the fixed level \(1-\alpha\).
